transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-02 15:30 UTC
Duration: 45m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Rivera (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (IvyPoint Head of MLOps), Priya Rao (IvyPoint Platform Eng), Ethan Morales (IvyPoint Finance), Sofia Kim (IvyPoint Security)

Auto-summary: customer wants to extend term and add EU region with dedicated capacity; needs SOC2/KMS confirmations and cost model for committed uplift. Agreed to run throughput benchmark and share pricing amendment.

Topics: capacity uplift request, EU onramp timeline, VPC/KMS, latency/cost tradeoff, procurement timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call — we got the agenda, we wanted to run through your request for the capacity bump and EU region onboarding,
[00:10] Liam O'Connor: yep thanks, maya, morning all, uh, short agenda from our side — need to lock in capacity before end of Q3, want to validate latency in eu and get pricing for committed uplift.
[00:22] Priya Rao: hi, we'll be the technical point — we care about VPC network pathing, egress cost, and KMS integration for key management.
[00:35] Jordan Patel: great — i'll lead the performance side — we've already prepped a test plan, we just need to know expected sequence lengths and concurrency ranges.
[00:45] Ethan Morales: and i'll focus on pricing and terms — curious about commitment tier discounts and any one-time region activation fees.
[00:52] Sofia Kim: security — SOC2 evidence, audit logs retention, and gap analysis for our internal compliance team.
[01:00] Maya Chen: perfect, i'll just put those into the roadmap — first question, liam, what's driving the 20% bump? is it new product lines or more throughput for existing endpoints?
[01:12] Liam O'Connor: it's a mix — we launched a routing assistant in july that's been steadily increasing token volume, and we expect a marketing push in oct. So we need predictable throughput and to avoid throttling in EU region.
[01:25] Jordan Patel: when you say routing assistant, are we talking long context windows? kv-cache heavy?
[01:30] Liam O'Connor: average prompt + history is around 750 tokens, but some flows hit 1.6k. Concurrency peaks around 200 rps across the EU clients.
[01:41] Jordan Patel: okay that's helpful — that sequence profile suggests batching will help but we need to look at tail-latency — are you currently on hosted or dedicated?
[01:49] Priya Rao: today on hosted for US, with a dedicated pool for a few high-traffic routes. We want dedicated in EU to meet our SLA.
[01:57] Maya Chen: right, dedicated in EU gives you more predictable throughput. There is an activation window of ~6–8 weeks typically for private onprem or VPC add-ons, hosted dedicated can be faster but less isolated.
[02:10] Sofia Kim: quick sec — for VPC we need to know KMS options. does redwood support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) in dedicated?
[02:18] Jordan Patel: yes, we support KMS integrations — there's a managed key path and a CMK/HSM option for Private deployments, though HSM requires a different onboarding checklist. Some transcriptions autocorrect it as H-S-M, so just flagging that — (laughs)
[02:33] Priya Rao: and what's the data residency model — if we put a dedicated EU pool, will logs/stats remain in region?
[02:40] Noah Rivera: logs can be routed and retained per region, we offer retention controls and audit log exports to your S3 in eu-west. We'll share the architecture doc.
[02:50] Ethan Morales: pricing — is region activation a one-time fee? and what discounts for a 12 vs 24 mo commitment?
[02:57] Maya Chen: region activation is a modest one‑time provisioning fee for dedicated pools; discounts scale by term and committed tokens / capacity. I'll attach a sample amendment showing +20% capacity with term extension and the effective blended rate.
[03:10] Liam O'Connor: timeline wise we need EU up and running by mid oct — is that feasible?
[03:16] Jordan Patel: if we go hosted-dedicated, probably yes within 2–3 weeks; private VPC/onprem with CMK may stretch to 6–8 weeks due to network and security reviews.
[03:27] Priya Rao: our security team prefers VPC with customer-managed KMS, but we can do a staged approach — start with hosted-dedicated for immediate latency gains, then migrate to VPC when the compliance sign-off lands.
[03:40] Maya Chen: that's a common approach — staged migration. We'll plan canary routing so you can split traffic gradually.
[03:45] Sofia Kim: what about SLAs — can we get latency SLOs per route if we move to dedicated?
[03:51] Jordan Patel: we publish p50/p90 numbers per model and per region in the console; dedicated pools can be configured with latency SLO guardrails and fallbacks to a lower-cost variant if pressure spikes. But fallbacks change model quality — we should enumerate which routes can tolerate fallback.
[04:08] Liam O'Connor: we'll map route criticality — the customer-facing assistant can't fallback, internal tooling can.
[04:14] Maya Chen: ok note to follow up on which route IDs are non-fallback.
[04:18] Priya Rao: for the benchmark session, we'll send representative payloads — we want a 30-min continuous test and some spike tests. Could you prepare a script?
[04:25] Jordan Patel: yep, we'll supply the artillery script and containerized runner. We'll also provide KV cache warmup steps because that materially affects sustained throughput.
[04:35] Ethan Morales: contract question — if we extend term plus +20% commitment, what's the billing cadence and any early termination adjustments?
[04:43] Maya Chen: billing can stay monthly against committed units; if you want pricing predictability, we can do annual prepay with deeper discounts. Early termination is handled in the amendment, typically pro-rated for committed capacity. I'll include language and examples.
[04:58] Sofia Kim: on SOC2, can you provide the latest Type II report and the architecture whitepaper? We need to run it through legal.
[05:05] Noah Rivera: yes — I'll share the SOC2 artifact link and the private deployment architecture. Expect a short readme outlining audit log retention and KMS specifics.
[05:15] Liam O'Connor: one more, we've been evaluating Anthropic for some flows — any hybrid routing recommendations if we keep Redwood for high-throughput and another provider for LLM diversity?
[05:25] Jordan Patel: we have routing policies that split by cost or latency; you can route lower-critical flows to other providers. Be mindful of tokens/format differences and output consistency. We can help with A/B checks.
[05:40] Priya Rao: ok good — so immediate plan: we want hosted-dedicated EU as a quick win and start onboarding VPC + CMK afterwards. Run the throughput benchmark next week. Maya will send pricing and amendment.
[05:52] Maya Chen: yes — i'll send pricing today, jordan will run tests and share results, noah will push SOC2 link to sofia. Anything else?
[06:00] Ethan Morales: procurement timeline — we need final numbers by Sep 10 to hit finance windows.
[06:05] Maya Chen: we'll aim for that.
[06:08] Liam O'Connor: thanks all — appreciate the quick sync.
[06:12] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with action items.
[06:15] -- End meeting --

References shared: pricing_amendment_draft_v2.xlsx (link: https://redwood.app/links/pricing-amend-ivy-49822), soc2_artifacts.zip (internal link), eu-dedicated-arch.pdf (link).

Notes on transcription quality: some proper nouns mis-recognized (IvyPoint sometimes appears as "ivy point"), technical acronyms occasionally expanded incorrectly (KV cache -> "K-v cache"), filler words and crosstalk present.

End of transcript.
